        Dear Robert Hoffman:

        Subject:        Receipt of Clean Water Act Section 401 Water Quality Certification
                        Request and Coastal Zone Management Act Consistency Certification:
                        Construction and Operation of Two SMR-300 Units at the Palisades
                        Energy Center, Covert Township, Van Buren County, Michigan (NRC
                        Project No. 99902049; Docket Nos. 050-616 and 050-617)

        The Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), Water Resources
        Division (WRD), has received a request for Water Quality Certification (WQC) pursuant
        to Section 401 of the Clean Water Act from Holtec International for the construction and
        operation of two Small Modular Reactor (SMR)-300 units at the Palisades Energy
        Center on the Lake Michigan coast in Covert Township, Van Buren County. The WQC
        request was received on April 7, 2026. This project requires a permit and license from
        the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and will result in a discharge to waters
        of the U.S.

        Additionally, this project has reasonably foreseeable effects on resources and uses of
        Michigan’s approved coastal management program area and is subject to Federal
        Consistency requirements under Section 307 of the Coastal Zone Management Act, PL
        92-583, as amended, and 15 CFR Part 930, Subpart D. EGLE WRD received the
        Consistency Certification with necessary data and information for this project from
        Holtec International pursuant to 15 CFR 930.57 on June 5, 2026. This date marks the
        beginning of the six-month Consistency Certification review period pursuant to 15 CFR
        930.60(a).

        Please note that Michigan’s water quality requirements that are applied to reviews of
        WQC requests are a subset of the approved enforceable policies of Michigan’s Coastal
        Management Program that are applied to reviews of Consistency Certifications.
        Consequently, many projects that require both WQC and Consistency Certification
        concurrence, such as the proposed construction and operation of the SMR-300 units,

are approved, denied, or approved with conditions developed by EGLE WRD based on
provisions of statutes and administrative rules that are both water quality requirements
and approved enforceable policies.

Pursuant to 40 CFR 121.6(b), EGLE WRD requests that the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission agree to a “reasonable period of time” for acting on the WQC request
through December 5, 2026. Such timeframe would allow EGLE WRD to fully coordinate
the WQC and Consistency Certification reviews of the lengthy and complex material
and complete public notice requirements.

If you have any questions regarding this letter, please contact me at 517-230-7849 or
SmarM@Michigan.gov.
